en: The Peta-Vatthu,
Great Chapter, 5.
The Story of the Sugarcane Ghost (Ucchu-peta-vatthu)
“This great field of sugarcane is mine,
producing no small fruit of merit;
yet now it does not come to my enjoyment.”
"Tell me, venerable sir, what is the result of this?
I am being struck and devoured; I strive, yet I am unable to enjoy anything."
"Alas, my strength is severed; I am a wretched man, lamenting.
Of what karma is this the ripening?
Oppressed and exhausted, I fall upon the ground."
I am turning over like a water-dweller in the heat;
tears flow from me as I weep.
Tell me, venerable sir, what is the result of this?
Hungry, exhausted, and thirsty, agitated,
I find no ease or happiness;
I ask you, O Blessed One, about this matter.
"How indeed might I obtain the enjoyment of sugar cane?
"In a former birth, when you were a human being, you yourself performed the deed."
And I speak this matter to you;
having heard this matter, understand it.
You have set out while eating sugarcane.
And a man followed behind you;
though he spoke to you as he sat facing you,
you did not say anything to him in reply.
And so, while he was not speaking, he entreated you,
saying, "Sir Deha, give me sugarcane";
and you gave him the sugarcane from behind his back.
This is the result of that karma.
Come now, go and seize him from behind;
having seized him, eat him as much as you desire.
"By that very means you shall be satisfied, joyful,
elated, and filled with delight. Having said this,
he went and seized him from behind.
Having taken it, he ate as much as he desired;
by that very act, he became satisfied,
joyful, elated, and filled with gladness.
The Fifth Story: Of Ucchuṣmavata.
